title: A partition of the rotation group into two sets each of which squares onto the whole group

core_obligations: Construct the partition (proof lines 968-970): let the first set consist of the rotations by rational radian values in [0, pi) and the second be its complement in the rotation group.

Show each part squares onto the whole group (proof lines 970-974): a rotation by s radians is the square of the rotation by s/2 radians, and when s/2 is rational at or beyond pi the rotation by s/2 minus pi, which lies in the first part, has the same square modulo a full turn; the author invokes this elementary algebra explicitly and notes the same argument for the second part.
proof_roadmap: Define the two parts by rationality of the radian measure (proof lines 968-970).
Verify both parts square onto the group by the half-angle computation (proof lines 970-974).
difficulty_reason: Partition construction plus a half-angle squaring computation the reader can check; the mechanism is explicit even though the author compresses the second part as similar, 7-line proof.
